Subject: MSA redlines — liability cap carve-out for trade secrets

Jonas / Laura —

Thanks for sending the draft MSA. Our procurement and legal teams reviewed; we have one narrow but critical ask around the liability cap: Calyx needs an explicit carve-out for breaches that lead to loss or misappropriation of trade secrets and willful exfiltration of Confidential Information.

Specifically: we need the cap not to apply where (i) there is willful or grossly negligent misuse of our trade secrets, or (ii) disclosure of Confidential Information that results in competitive harm. We also want a mechanism to preserve relevant evidence so we can evaluate damages (logs, access history, retained payloads).

I've attached our redlines and a short list of forensic items we expect to receive in the event of an incident. Can Redwood confirm you can commit to providing those artifacts within 14 days post-notice?

Attachments: Calyx_MSA_Redlines_20261103.pdf; TradeSecret_Evidence_Reqs.docx

Best,
Samantha Ortiz
VP, Procurement — Calyx Health

Thanks for the clear ask and the redlines. Looping in Laura (legal) to confirm feasibility. Subject: Fwd: MSA redlines — liability cap carve-out for trade secrets

Jonas / team —

Quick note after reviewing Calyx's proposed text and their evidence checklist. We're willing to accept a carve-out for: (A) judicially determined misappropriation of trade secrets, and (B) intentional exfiltration of Confidential Information by Redwood personnel or willful misuse of the platform. Proposed gating language: removal of cap only upon (i) criminal conviction, (ii) civil judgment for misappropriation, or (iii) a final written determination by an independent arbitrator.

On preservation: operations can preserve and produce the following items within 14 calendar days after Redwood receives a valid preservation notice and completes necessary legal verifications: (1) audit logs (access/auth events), (2) per-request payload hashes and timestamps, (3) model KV-cache snapshots for the relevant timeframe (when applicable), and (4) infrastructure-level telemetry for the session IDs in question.

We should be explicit about what Redwood will not produce (raw customer prompts from other customers, raw model weights, or any unrelated customer data). Also we need Calyx to cover reasonable costs associated with forensic collection if we need to engage external specialists beyond our standard support scope.

Marissa / David — please confirm operational lead and point of contact for evidence delivery; also note we should add a clause limiting retention requests to incidents where Calyx provides a prima facie showing of a confidentiality incident (to avoid broad fishing).

-Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Rajiv (incoming) will be our outside counsel and will help us shape the exact carve-out wording and the affidavit verbiage. If you're ok, let's schedule a short call later this week to iron out retention windows and the evidence delivery checklist.
